summary:
**EARTHSONIC – Listen to What Earth Is Telling Us**

EARTHSONIC is a web-based prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, inspired by the idea of making Earth science more accessible through sound.

The project converts visual features of NASA Earth visualizations into audio, allowing users to explore images in a different way. As a scanline moves across an image, the system translates brightness, colour and position into changes in sound, pitch and stereo movement.

Users can explore NASA visualizations, select images, play or pause the audio, adjust playback speed and control volume. The goal is to provide a more engaging and accessible way to experience information about our planet, especially for people who may have difficulty interpreting visual content.

EARTHSONIC is an early prototype that demonstrates how sound can create a new connection between people and Earth's visual data. It is a step towards making scientific information more interactive and inclusive.
details:
EARTHSONIC is a web-based prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Its main idea is to make Earth science more accessible by converting visual information into sound.

The project allows users to explore NASA Earth visualizations and listen to how different visual features are translated into audio. As a scanline moves across a selected image, the system analyses its pixels and maps their brightness, colour and horizontal position to sound characteristics such as pitch, tone, intensity and stereo movement. Users can play, pause, restart and control the speed and volume of the audio.

The main benefit of EARTHSONIC is that it offers a different way to experience scientific visualizations, particularly for people who are blind or have low vision. It can also help other users explore Earth imagery in a more interactive and engaging way.

Our intended impact is to encourage inclusive access to Earth science and demonstrate how sound can complement visual scientific information. We hope this concept can inspire further development of accessible tools for exploring our planet.

We developed the prototype using React and JavaScript for the frontend, Node.js and Express for the backend, and HTML and CSS for the interface. We used NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS) resources to access Earth-related visualizations. The audio generation is handled through browser-based audio technologies, without requiring additional hardware.

The creative aspect of EARTHSONIC is its approach of turning visual patterns into an audio experience. Instead of only looking at an image, users can listen to its changing visual characteristics through a moving scanline.

During development, our team considered accessibility, ease of use, cost, browser compatibility and the accuracy of the information presented. We also considered the difference between sonifying image properties and representing actual scientific measurements. The current prototype focuses on image-based sonification and is an initial step towards a more complete accessible Earth science experience.
